question: The headwaters of the river Ganga is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is Bhagirathi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gangotri Glacier feeds the "Bhagirathi," Ganga's headwaters.**
 
• At **Devaprayag in Uttarakhand,** the** Alaknanda joins it**.
 
• The **Ganga** leaves the mountains and enters the plains in **Haridwar**.
 
• A number of significant rivers, including the **Yamuna, the Ghaghara, the Gandak, and the Kosi,** join the **Ganga** from the **Himalayas**.
 
• The **Ganges** is thought to have its origins in the **Bhagirathi in Hindu mythology and culture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandakini**

 
 
• ​In the **Indian state of Uttarakhand**, the** Mandakini River** is a** tributary of the Alaknanda River**.
 
• The river emerges from the **Chorabari** **Glacier** and flows for around 81 kilometres (50 miles) between the **Rudraprayag and Sonprayag regions.**
 
• The river passes past the Hindu shrine **Madhyamaheshwar** at **Ukhimath** before joining the river** Songanga at Sonprayag.**
 
 
 
• **Alaknanda**
 
 
• ​The **Alaknanda** is one of the **two headstreams of the Ganges**, the principal river of Northern India and the holy river of Hinduism.
 
• It originates in the **Himalayas** and flows through the** Indian state of Uttarakhand.**
 
• Due to its longer length and flow, the **Alaknanda** is regarded as the **Ganges**' source stream in hydrology; yet, in Hindu tradition and culture, the **Bhagirathi**, the other headstream, is regarded as the source stream.
